parsed.explanation: No documented traveller-facing criminalisation, facility ban, border rejection, police targeting, or trans-specific killing pattern. Self-declaration recognition, a 2024 hate-crime act covering gender identity, incitement protections, open Pride/venues, and 61% public support indicate a protective climate with functioning recourse. Counterweights are rising reported discrimination and hate crimes, a resident healthcare bottleneck and denials, no nonbinary domestic marker for an X passport, and a first-stage-only proposal on imprisonment certificates. These raise friction and uncertainty, not a documented severe traveller exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: X passport has no domestic equivalent; treatment at entry is not documented.
entry_documents.protection: Self-declaration recognition since 2015 signals accepting document practice; no restriction on foreign documents documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could prompt questioning, but no documented refusal or detention pattern.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One custodial case involving a certificate holder; amendment limiting certificates for imprisonment passed only first stage, not enacted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented birth-sex custody policy or pattern of trans detention for identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If detained for unrelated reasons, placement effect of the unpassed proposal remains uncertain.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented bathroom, ward, or facility exclusion rule reaches visitors in this record.

care_services.exposure: Resident waits 2.5-10 years and documented denials at single provider; visitor continuity, import, or emergency placement not documented.
care_services.protection: Gender-affirming care is legal; national service defends multidisciplinary model.
care_services.interaction: Resident bottleneck is a climate and continuity risk, not a documented visitor refusal.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: University study July 2025 reports increasing discrimination/prejudice despite protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Criminal Justice (Hate Offences) Act 2024 covers gender identity; incitement act adds gender identity with penalties.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Strong statutory framing coexists with rising social prejudice; no state threat-framing of trans presence documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care restricted for minors for residents; 2019 council cancelled drag storytime citing age and online abuse.
minors_guardians.protection: 2019 ministerial recommendation for 16-17 recognition with parental consent was not enacted; no visitor-minor restriction documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's care or school access is uncertain, but no traveller-facing ban is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Hate crimes reported up 15% in 2025, but racism/xenophobia most common and no trans-specific rate or killing documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Visible Pride, venues nationwide, formal apologies in 2018, and hate-crime reporting route.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: General rise and discrimination suggest occasion al friction, not organised targeting or impunity pattern.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: X-marker handling, visitor care access, and custody placement under proposed amendment are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anonymous hate-crime reporting form, equality-status information, and 2024 hate-offence statute provide recourse signals.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies appear formally available, but no documented visitor case shows their speed or outcome.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: explicit protective law, oversight/reporting, broad tolerance, residual friction. This case scores slightly lower due to documented rising discrimination and healthcare denial evidence, and X-marker uncertainty.

Higher than this anchor: there is no documented border detention discretion, document-fraud detention, or compensation-dependent remedy; risks are mainly social friction and continuity, not secondary inspection.

Materially higher: care problems are resident waiting/denial, not a documented visitor refusal overturned on complaint, and there is no custodial threat or repeated exposure of clinical privacy for visitors.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is nationally protective with no documented universal traveller exposure: entry, facilities, detention and policing show no operative hostile rule, while hate-crime law and open social infrastructure provide mitigation. The operative risks are secondary: increasing prejudice, general hate-crime reporting growth, resident care delays that may affect continuity, uncertain X-passport practice, and an unpassed custodial-certificate proposal. Rule-of-law protections appear to operate formally, so social friction is discounted somewhat, but unproven remedies for the open questions prevent a near-perfect score.
